_comment: Speeds keep a 30:20:18:35:22 ratio, scaled so a Scooter 10 sails Rome-Tunis in about 60 s. range_nm is the longest single leg the model can sail (Scooter 10: 1 min 30 s of sailing, GE 100: 3 min 30 s, Greenline 200: 6 min, Trans Atlantic: Rome to New York, Dominator: 9,000 nm). max_owned is how many of each model the player can own. map_size (length, width in pixels) and map_color are how the ship is drawn on the map: container ships run yellow to red and gas tankers light green to dark blue (smallest to biggest), recovery boats brown (darker = bigger). breakdown_factor scales the chance of a random breakdown (bigger ships are sturdier). fuel_tank is in fuel units; fuel_per_s is burned every second at sea, whatever the speed. Burn was set so fuel cost about a third of a leg's pay at full speed (about 40% since the fuel price rose 20%), and tanks are sized so a ship leaving at 100% maintenance can just finish a range_nm leg (plus 1 s spare) while wearing and slowing on the way. Recovery boats (recovery: true) sail no routes: they recover lost ships, and range_nm is the longest recovery job they can do. carries lists the models a recovery boat can carry (none listed = any). The Mammoth costs the most to run; the Mini Mammoth, the size of a Trans Atlantic, carries only Scooter 10s, GE 100s, Greenline 200s and Coastal tankers and costs about a tenth as much to run. wear_pct_per_min is maintenance lost per minute of running at sea (the Dominator and Mammoth wear at half rate; speed is top speed x maintenance, so a ship at 0% stops); repair_cost_per_pct is set so repairs cost about 10% of what the ship earns sailing. dock_s is how long a ship unloads and loads at each port; repair, then refuel, each take refill_phase_s of that time. category groups the models in the shop: container ships, gas tankers and recovery boats. Gas tankers carry fuel as paid cargo: capacity is tons of fuel, paid at pay_per_unit_nm (container ships use game_config pay_per_container_nm); each size is 10x the cargo and 15% slower than the last. unlock_level is the company level needed to buy the model. xp_first_level is the ship XP a cargo ship needs for its first level; each level after costs 5% more (game_config ship_level_growth). Bigger models need disproportionately more, so small ships level fastest.
